Volta Daily Report — original spreadsheet layout

Yesterday and MTD side by side, exactly like the Volta_Analytics Report tab. Tap a yellow/orange section header to collapse it.

Source: from August 31 on, every metric comes from the new database (VoltaStoreDB) — Applications/Terms/Underwriting are keyed to the application date (created_at), Downpayment Collected to the payment date (actually collected, not just recorded), Deals Closed/Amount Sold to the date the loan reaches Active status (crm_activity_log, Signed→Active; this concept doesn't exist before August 31, where the old Order_Date is used instead); amount = the full installment amount: product price + financing markup, i.e. the payment schedule total — before August 31, the old Full_Cost, where price and full amount are the same because of 0% installments). History before August 31 comes from the old database (myvolta.info). Note: from August 31 on, the old database no longer records Underwriting/Downpayment/Order Date (deals are closed in the new CRM instead), so the old dashboard shows 0 in these rows for September — here you see the real numbers. Applications here run slightly higher than in the old one (e.g. MTD 421 vs 360), because applications created directly in the new CRM no longer appear in the old database.

MTD Statistics — same report, one column per month

Same Section A/B/C layout as the Report tab, but pivoted: each column pair is one calendar month of 2026 instead of Yesterday/MTD. Scroll right for more months. Tap a section header to collapse it.

Daily Statistics — same report, one column per day

Same Section A/B/C layout as the Report tab, but pivoted: each column pair is one calendar day from June 1, 2026 through yesterday. Click a month header below to collapse its days.

Full Sales Funnel — from website sessions to signed cases

One column per calendar month of 2026 (the current month is month-to-date, through yesterday). Website sessions are the month's traffic; every other row is the applications submitted in that month and the status each of them was in at the end of yesterday (today's changes are not in yet) — a recent month keeps moving on refresh as its applications get decided. Three gates, in the order a case travels: sales screen the applications first (3 rejected by sales, 3.1 still with sales / unreachable / expired, 4 the customer withdrew there) and pass the rest on to the committee (5); the committee rejects (6), leaves some waiting (6.1), loses some to the customer (7) and approves the rest (8); of the approved, 8.1 fall out on Volta's side, 9 are declined by the customer and the rest are signed (10, together with the single-payment sales that need no underwriting). Each percentage row names its base. Main stages shows only the numbered stages; Detailed breakdown adds the reasons and the sub-stage items. Tap a section header to collapse it.

Sales Monthly — by product category

One column-group (Sales / Cogs / Margin / Qty) per calendar month of 2026, plus Q1 and Q2 quarterly summary groups (each with that row's share of the quarter's total Sales) and an overall Total group (share of the whole window). Installment sales use the "real sale" status (Order_Status = 5 / crm_order_status = 5); single-payment sales use Type_Of_Sales = 99 / crm_order_status = 99, keyed to the application date since they have no order date. Rows are sorted by total Sales, highest first. Sales = SUM(Final_Price), Cogs = SUM(Start_Price), both raw and unmodified — same convention the business's own report uses.

Brand Analyze — by brand

Same layout as Sales Monthly, grouped by brand instead of product category. On the old DB the brand link is fully populated; on the new DB brand is a product attribute that is missing on part of the catalog, so the "No Brand" row grows from the cutover on (see the note below the table). Three "no real brand" spellings (none, N/A, ბრენდის გარეშე) are combined into one "No Brand" row at the bottom.

Subcategory Analyze — by broader product group

Same layout as Sales Monthly, but one level broader — e.g. Air Fryer / Blender / Toaster (separate rows on Sales Monthly) all roll up into one "Small Kitchen Appliances" row here. Same mapping-sheet lookup as Sales Monthly, just reading its Subcategory(EN) field instead of Product(EN).

Category / Brand — brand breakdown within each category

One block per product category, brands broken down within it — same layout as the business's own reference report's "Top 4 — Brands" sheet, built here for every category found in the window instead of a hand-picked top 4. Q1/Q2 Sales are date-bounded quarterly columns; Total Sales/COGS/Margin/Qty are for the whole window (Jan 1–yesterday), matching the reference sheet's own formulas. Categories and brands within them are sorted by Total Sales, highest first (Uncategorized/No Brand always last).

Logistics Daily — PO & Order Fulfillment

Sales – Pending Status = loan applications submitted from 1 September 2026 on that are still in the "Pending" status (crm_order_status = 4) at the end of each day, by how long they have been open (days since submission). The CRM's own Pending figure is ~360 higher because it also counts applications from December 2025 – August 2026 migrated from the old CRM that were never closed; those are left out here on purpose. Reconstructed exactly from the CRM's status-change log, so every day since the cutover is real history, not a snapshot; the last column is today as of the last refresh.

Not Delivered = active orders in the CRM logistics module with no delivered / picked-up event yet at the end of that day (an order enters the series on its sale date, or on the day the module picked it up if that was later); age buckets (≤1 day / 1–5 days / >5 days) are measured from the sale date. Delivered = orders whose first delivered or picked-up event (CRM logistics status 80/81) fell on that day; Average Delivery Time = average days from sale to that event. "On Hold" has no equivalent in the new CRM yet and stays blank. All rows are reconstructed from the CRM's shipment-status history.

Open Cases — Still Waiting for Delivery (today)

The 10 oldest active orders (by sale date) with no delivered / picked-up event — the customers who have been waiting longest. Status = the CRM logistics stage of the order.

CRM Logistics — Status by Day

The same stages the CRM's Logistics page shows ("Lines by status" and the order / collection stages), as they stood at the end of each day. Orders = one row per order in the logistics module (crm_order_logistics); Order lines = each product line's own fulfillment stage (crm_line_fulfillment, what the CRM's "Lines by status" counts); Vendor collections = pickup runs from vendors (crm_vendor_collections). "Partially ready" = an order whose lines are at different stages. Reconstructed from the CRM's shipment-status history. Same population as every table on this tab (orders in the logistics module in the CRM statuses Signed or Active), so the Orders total equals ALL Orders in the city / goods tables and Delivered + Picked up equals ALL Orders minus Not Delivered. "Signed, not yet Active" = the CRM's Signed status: the contract is signed and logistics has started, the deal moves to Active a few hours later (on average 4 hours, at most a few days); it is a memo line inside the Total, not an addition to it. Lines outnumber orders because an order with several products has one line per product.

Orders by City
Orders by Goods Type

City = the order's shipping address (Tbilisi / other cities / no city recorded). Goods Type = the product's top-level category from the mapping sheet (the old sheet's Soft / Medium / Heavy weight classes do not exist in the new catalog); each order is counted once, under the goods type of its highest-value product line. Not Delivered = orders in the module with no delivered / picked-up event yet at the end of that day; ALL Orders = every order that had entered the logistics module by the end of that day (delivered ones included). Same rules as the Delivery Status table, so the Not Delivered totals match it day by day. The last columns of each table carry the shares: each row's share of the total on the last day, and (in the ALL Orders table) the orders that entered the module during the last day's calendar month with their share.

Procurement & Logistics — Time in Each Status

Status Statistics — by Month, City and Vendor

Same orders as the table below, after the filters above. Average / Median time: how long orders stayed in each status (completed stays only, as in the Average row below; hover a cell for how many orders it is based on); Total = signed to delivered / picked up, delivered orders only. Orders by current status: where those orders stand right now (hover a cell for its share of the row). Month = the month the order entered logistics. By vendor: an order with items from several vendors is counted under each of them (its times are order-level, so it adds the same times to every vendor it has).

Order by Order

One row per order that entered the logistics module from September 1 (newest first; the module went live on September 2). Each status column = how long the order stayed in that status before moving to the next one, i.e. how long that step took: Started = until the order was sent to the vendor, Ordered from vendor = until the vendor confirmed it was ready, Ready at vendor = until a collection was booked, Collection scheduled = until it was picked up from the vendor, Collected = until it arrived at the warehouse, At warehouse = until it was ready to ship, Ready to ship = until it went out to the customer, Out for delivery = until the customer received it. Signed → logistics start = from the contract being signed (CRM status Signed) to the logistics module picking the order up. A status visited more than once is summed (hover a cell for every visit with its start and end). Highlighted cells are the status the order is in right now, counted up to the snapshot time and still growing. Total = signed (or logistics start) to delivered / picked up / cancelled, or to the snapshot time if still open. Times are calendar time (nights and weekends included), clock times are Tbilisi time. Average row = completed stays only. Statuses marked "?" have no name in the CRM's data; the label is our reading of where those orders go next. * after the order number = items from several vendors.

Profit Margins — by product category, September 2026

Two margins side by side, both for September only, both from VoltaStoreDB (the old database and August are no longer used here at all). Sorted by Site Price, highest first.

September 2026: Site Price vs Purchase Price  |  Installment Total vs Site Price

Site Price (both halves) is each product line's own price on that September order (order_items.base_total) — never a different month, never a different database, so there's no matching or bridging of any kind anywhere in this tab. Site Price vs Purchase Price: installment sales only; Purchase Price = the product's cost (a real field, product_attribute_values, attribute "cost"), scoped to only the lines that have one so the two sides stay comparable; Margin = Site Price − Purchase Price, % of Site Price. Installment Total vs Site Price: installment loans only (single-payment has no schedule); Installment Total = what the customer is contracted to pay (crm_installment_schedules summed, plus the advance when it isn't already inside the schedule), allocated to each line by its share of the order's site-price total; Margin = Installment Total − Site Price, % of Site Price.

Product Sales — by Category › Subcategory › Product, month by month

Each product sits under its Subcategory, which sits under its Category (same mapping sheet as Sales Monthly, so the grand total is identical). Category and Subcategory rows are subtotals — click one to collapse or expand what is under it. Product rows are sorted by total Sales within their group, highest first.

Marketing — Leads

Leads by status

Flow. New leads = rows of volta_leads (the pre-application lead form on the website) counted on the day / month they were created (created_at, UTC day like the rest of the dashboard). Rows = the lead's current status in the CRM (volta_leads.status, the CRM's marketing statuses New / Contacted / Qualified / Won / Lost): the table does not record when a lead changed status — a lead created in June and contacted in September is counted as Contacted in June. The CRM only started working leads on 2026-08-31 (the first sales-manager assignments), so practically every earlier lead still says New. Memo rows: leads with a sales manager (crm_sales_manager_id), and leads whose phone number had already sent a lead before (repeat submissions are counted as leads in every row). Deleted leads (CRM lead.delete) disappear from the table retroactively. Day tables: share of the last day, plus the last 7 days and their share; month tables: share of the current month, plus the all-time total and its share.

Leads by form step

Flow. The same leads by the last step of the lead form the visitor reached (last_step 1–3; step 3 = the form was completed). From 2026-09-02 no lead reaches step 2 or 3 any more: the form was changed with the new CRM and now records one step only, so the step split is only meaningful up to 2026-09-01. Keyed to the lead creation date.

Leads by city

Flow. The same leads by the city the visitor typed (free text: Georgian and Latin spellings are folded together; the six biggest cities are shown, everything else is Other Cities, empty = Without City). Keyed to the lead creation date.

Lead → application conversion

Flow, keyed to the lead creation date. The CRM does not link a lead to the application it turned into (orders.crm_source_lead_id is never filled), so the link is made by phone number: a lead is matched to every application (orders) whose billing-address phone (addresses, order_billing) or customer record (customers.phone / volta_leads.customer_id) carries the same number. Applications after the lead = at least one application created at or after the lead; within 30 days = created within 30 days of the lead (the last 30 days of leads are still open, so their 30-day rate is incomplete); Loans issued = one of those applications became a loan (crm_order_status 5 Active or 99 single payment, or crm_active = 1) — the lead is counted once whichever way it matched. "Already a customer" = the phone had an application before the lead (an existing customer using the form). Rates are the share of that day's / month's leads. Applications before 2026-08-31 are the rows migrated from the old CRM, whose created_at can be a day off; the phone match itself is exact. A lead whose applicant used another phone number is not matched, so the rates are a floor, not a ceiling. Day tables: last 7 days; month tables: all-time total.

Operations — Applications

Applications by current status

Flow, keyed to the application date (orders.created_at, UTC calendar day like every other tab): the loan applications submitted on that day / in that month, split by the status they are in today (orders.crm_order_status) — a snapshot of where each cohort stands, not what happened on that day. Rows are the CRM statuses (legend below); the last columns give each status's share of the last day / of the current month. Month columns start at January 2026: the application rows exist for all of 2026 (migrated from the old CRM), only the status history is missing before September. Applications here run slightly above the Daily Mail tab for the migrated months (e.g. January 1,858 vs 1,817) because Daily Mail takes those months from the old database.

Status changes – applications entering each status

Flow, keyed to the day of the status change: how many status changes moved an application into each status that day / month, from the CRM's own audit trail (crm_activity_log, action = 'installment.status_change', JSON metadata.to). An application that passes through several statuses counts once in each; one that is returned and resubmitted counts twice in the same status. The trail starts on 1 September 2026 — nothing before it exists in the new database, so the month series has only the months since then.

Funnel by application date – where the applications stand today

State, keyed to the application date: of the applications submitted that day / month, how many are approved by the committee today (crm_underwriter_status_id = 16), signed or active (crm_order_status 11 / 5 / 1), still in process, rejected, declined by the customer or expired. The last column is the share of that day's / month's applications. Recent columns are still moving (the cohort is being worked); older months are settled. "Signed or Active" contains "of which Active"; the remaining rows (still in process, rejected, declined, expired, other) add up to the applications.

Status codes — what was verified

English labels are ours; the CRM wording is the exact text the CRM writes into the audit trail on each status change ("სტატუსის შეცვლა: …"), so every status that occurs in the live flow is verified from the system itself. Pending / Signed / Active are the names the CRM's Applications page shows. Codes 3 and 14 occur only on migrated rows and have no wording anywhere in the database — they are shown as unverified. Observed order of the flow: 4 → 7 → 8 → 16 → 17 → 9 → 10 → 11 → Active (log code 1, stored as 5); 8 → 15 → 8 is a return for clarification; 6 / 12 / 13 are the terminal negative outcomes.

Operations — Committee

Committee decisions by decision date

Flow, keyed to the decision timestamp in the audit trail: every status change out of "At committee" (8) — Approved (→ 16), Returned for clarification (→ 15) or Rejected (→ 6). The lime row is the total of the three; the approval rate is approved ÷ decisions. Memo rows: applications sent to the committee that day (→ 8, including resubmissions after a clarification), and the stock at the end of the day / month — applications still sitting at the committee (status 8) or waiting for the requested clarification (status 15), reconstructed from the trail (today's figures equal the live CRM counts). orders.crm_approve_date is not written by the new CRM (it is NULL on 183 of 189 post-cutover approvals), so the audit-trail timestamp is the only decision date. One application can carry more than one decision (returned, then approved): 489 decisions on 426 applications so far.

Underwriting outcome by application date

State, keyed to the application date: the applications submitted that day / month by their underwriting status today (orders.crm_underwriter_status_id: 16 approved, 15 clarification needed, 6 rejected, NULL = no decision recorded). Last column = share of that period's applications. Caution on the "Rejected (6)" row: the CRM stamps underwriting status 6 on every rejection, including the ones sales managers make before the case reaches the committee (status 4 → 6 and 7 → 6), so it is "rejected at any stage", not "rejected by the committee" — the committee's own rejections are in the decisions table above and the reasons table below.

Decisions per underwriter

Flow, keyed to the decision timestamp: the same decisions out of status 8, by the CRM user who made them (audit-trail actor, joined to crm_users; the two people with the Underwriter role make nearly all of them, the odd sales-manager row is a case closed by sales while it sat at the committee). The day table counts decisions; the month table splits them into approved / returned / rejected with the approval rate. orders.crm_underwriter_id is deliberately not used: the CRM also writes it with whichever sales manager rejects a case before committee ("Underwriter assigned by deciding the case"), so it would attribute pre-committee rejections to sales staff.

Committee rejection reasons

Flow, keyed to the rejection timestamp: rejections made at the committee stage (from status 8, or from 15 after a clarification request) by the reason the underwriter selected — the text after "მიზეზი:" in the audit-trail summary (the same value lands in orders.crm_reason). Standard reasons are listed by their CRM wording with an English gloss; anything typed free-hand is "Other (free text)". Last column = share of the period's committee rejections.

All rejections by stage

Flow, keyed to the rejection timestamp: every status change to Rejected (6), by the status the application was in when it was rejected — screened out by sales while Pending (4) or In processing (7), rejected by the committee (8) or after a clarification request (15), or cancelled after approval (16 / 17 / 9 / 10, typically duplicates). Puts the committee's rejections in proportion to the rest.

Customers Analyze — who applies and who borrows

Customer = a distinct person, identified by the personal ID typed on the application form, else the ID number on the customer account (together of applications; the account id or the e-mail for the rest). Application = one orders row by its application date (created_at). Active loan = crm_active = 1 and not a pending application. Loan = an application that became an installment or single-payment sale (crm_order_status 5 / 99, a closed loan, or an active one). Every table is an aggregate — no names, phones or ID numbers are stored in this page.

New vs returning applicants — by month

New vs returning applicants — by day

Applications and loans per customer

How many applications (left) and how many loans (right) each customer has had, all time. A customer with 0 loans applied but never borrowed. "With active loan" = customers in that bucket who have an active loan today.

Gender

Gender as answered on the application form (volta_application_data.gender; migrated applications carry the old CRM value, web applications the form value); the customer account's gender is the fallback.

Age

Age from the birth date on the application form (birth_date; the account's date_of_birth as fallback) — never from the ID number. Customer columns = age today; the by-month table = age on the application date. Ages outside 14–100 are treated as missing.

Geography (city of the shipping address)

City of the order's shipping address (addresses.city, address_type = order_shipping) — the 15 most frequent cities, the rest grouped as Other cities. The new DB has no region field.

Employment status

Employment status selected on the web application form (employment_status: private sector / self-employed / public sector / unemployed). The field exists only on applications submitted through the web form since 12 March 2026; migrated applications do not carry it, hence "Not on the form". Present on ~95% of web applications March–August 2026; since the 31 Aug 2026 cutover the new form records it on only a minority of applications (~15% in September), so the latest month is thin.

Social status

Social status selected on the web application form (social_status: housewife / student / pensioner; left empty = none of these). On the form since 12 March 2026, like employment status. Present on ~95% of web applications March–August 2026; since the 31 Aug 2026 cutover the new form records it on only a minority of applications (~15% in September), so the latest month is thin.

Monthly income (declared salary, GEL)

Salary declared on the web application form (salary, a number since February 2026; for ~1,200 March–April 2026 applications a range picked from a list, mapped to the same bands). Self-declared, not verified. Migrated applications do not carry it. Present on ~95% of web applications March–August 2026; since the 31 Aug 2026 cutover the new form records it on only a minority of applications (~15% in September), so the latest month is thin.

How the customer heard about Volta

"How did you hear about us" on the web application form (about_us_source), on the form since January 2026. "Used Volta before" is the applicant's own answer — compare it with the New / Returning tables, which are computed from the application history. Present on ~95% of web applications March–August 2026; since the 31 Aug 2026 cutover the new form records it on only a minority of applications (~15% in September), so the latest month is thin.

Risk status (CRM)

CRM risk status of the loan (orders.crm_risk_status: დაბალი / low = Low, საშუალო / medium = Medium, მაღალი = High; 0 / empty = not rated). It is set when a loan is issued, so applications that never became a loan are mostly "Not rated". Customer columns use the status of the customer's active loan (else the latest rated loan).

Job title (free text, top 15)

Job title typed on the application form (position, ~7,600 distinct raw values) — the 15 most frequent exact values, everything else under Other. Not clustered on purpose (spelling variants stay separate).

Customer rating (CRM profile, 1–5)

Star rating on the CRM customer profile (crm_customer_profile.rating, migrated from the old CRM; 0 = not rated), linked to the customer through the account or the ID number. Only a small part of the base is rated — see the coverage line.

Portfolio Analyze — the loan book by day and by month

Portfolio size — end-of-day stock

Stock at the end of each day (last column = today as of the last refresh). Active loans = installment loans disbursed by the end of that day and not closed by then (orders with crm_order_status 5, or 1 on rows migrated from the old CRM; disbursement date = crm_creator_date; closure = crm_close_date, or the last payment date when the close was never recorded or its date is a placeholder). Outstanding balance = what those loans still owe: today it is exactly the schedule balance (crm_installment_schedules: schedule − paid, which equals orders.grand_total); for earlier days it is today's balance plus the principal the loans paid after that day (crm_payments, reversed payments and one 99,999,999.99 placeholder excluded) — a reconstruction, exact to the extent the payment ledger is. Contract amount = the full installment amount (schedule total + advance, the Daily Mail "Amount Sold" rule); product price = base_grand_total.

Portfolio size — month-end stock

The same stock at each month-end from 2025-01 (last column = today, i.e. the current month to date). Months before the cutover (2026-08-31) are reconstructed from rows migrated on the cutover day: their disbursement dates drift by hours to a few days from the old CRM's order dates and their closure dates come from the recorded close or the last payment, so the month-end counts are close but not to-the-loan exact; from the cutover on everything is real history. The old CRM stopped recording closes in June 2026 — loans that finished paying between then and the cutover have no close record and are treated as closed on their last payment day.

Portfolio flows — by day

Flows on each day. Disbursed = loans whose disbursement date (crm_creator_date) is that day — the same population as Daily Mail's Deals Closed / Amount Sold (active loans by sale date), extended with the loans that were disbursed and have since been closed; contract amount, product price and advance (crm_advance_amount) as in Daily Mail. Average term = schedule rows per loan (the advance row of a migrated 11-row schedule is not a month); average advance % = advance ÷ product price over loans that carry an advance (migrated loans carry none, so before the cutover this reads "–"). Closed = loans whose closure fell on that day: paid off with a recorded close (crm_close_type 1, keyed to crm_close_date), paid off without a close record (schedule fully paid, keyed to the last payment date), written off (crm_close_type 2; amount = balance written off, the schedule balance still open on those loans). Net change = disbursed − closed, and equals the day-to-day change of the Active loans stock above. Single-payment sales (crm_order_status 99) are a memo line, not part of the book.

Portfolio flows — by month

The same flows by calendar month from 2025-01 (last column = current month to date). Before the cutover the disbursement month comes from migrated crm_creator_date values (month totals reconcile with the old dashboard within a few percent; days do not), closures from recorded close dates (garbage dates such as 1924/1970 or dates before disbursement are replaced by the last payment date) or, where none was recorded, the last payment date. Written-off loans were booked in bulk (Jan 2026), not month by month.

Structure of the loans disbursed each month

Loans by term, contract amount, segment, goods type, city and risk — by month of disbursement

Each table counts the loans disbursed in each month (same population as the Disbursed row above) by one attribute; the trailing columns give each row's share of the current month, the total over the whole window and its share. Term = number of monthly schedule rows. Contract amount = the full installment amount. Segment A = the product name starts with ტელეფონი / ტელევიზორ or the order is over 2,500 GEL (the Daily Mail rule). Goods type = the mapping sheet's top-level category of the loan's highest-value product line (src/product_mapping.json; catalog categories the sheet does not know land in Uncategorized). City = the order's shipping address (addresses, order_shipping). Risk status = crm_risk_status as stored (Georgian and English spellings merged; "0" / empty = not scored).

Vintage — how the loans of each disbursement month stand today

One row per disbursement month: loans disbursed and their contract amount; how many are still active today, paid off (with or without a close record) or written off; the balance still outstanding on the active ones and its share of the month's contract amount. A young month is mostly active; a month older than the typical 10-month term is mostly paid off — what remains active there is late.

The active book today (2026-10-05)

Point-in-time snapshot of every active loan (crm_active = 1) as of the last refresh: count, contract amount, outstanding balance and the row's share of the balance. Months remaining = crm_remaining_months as stored by the CRM; loan age = full months since disbursement. Overdue buckets, collections and payments are on the Collections tab, not here.

Data notes
